transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thank you for the follow-up! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

So gentle gardening is fine from week one onwards, just take it easy and avoid anything too demanding.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's good to know. My next question is: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

Your medication and drops should be stored as directed on the bottle - so check whether it needs to go in the fridge or at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the clarification. Yes, I have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light; is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses, and it should improve over time. If it's mild, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. I had my surgery about a week ago, so I'll give it a bit more time like you suggested. I don't have any more questions for now. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you so much for your assistance.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
